chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: The adhān and the iqāmah are thirty-five phrases. He counted that with his hand one by one: the adhān is eighteen phrases, and the iqāmah is seventeen phrases.

key_terms.الْأَذَانُ: the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: the call declaring the immediate commencement of salat (prayer)
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ: the number of phrases in the adhān
key_terms.حَرْفًا: here meaning counted units or phrases of the formula
key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ: the total number of phrases in the adhān and iqāmah combined
key_terms.سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ: the number of phrases in the iqāmah

ai.seo_question: How many phrases are there in the adhān and iqāmah according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the number of phrases in the adhān and the iqāmah, specifying that together they total thirty-five. It presents a legal and ritual teaching from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the proper form of these acts of worship.
